newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine call rate slips on adequate peso supply.
newsitem.headline: Philippine call rate slips on adequate peso supply.

text.p: The Philippine interbank call loan rate slipped to 11.0625 percent from Monday's 11.125 percent after demand eased due to ample peso supply, traders said.
"There was no excitement in the market today. The supply easily covered the demand," one trader said.
The system received a net inflow of fresh funds last week after maturing bills exceeded awards in the auction.
The average interbank rate was slightly above the 11.0 percent benchmark rate of the Central Bank. Done rates were wedged between 11.03125 percent and 11.25 percent.
Turnover shrank to 19.725 billion pesos from yesterday's 21.100 billion pesos, the trader added.
Bankers were not worried about the softening peso against the dollar, saying the recent dollar-buying spree would ease with foreign funds coming back to the local stock market.
Secondary rates of government securities were hovering slightly lower than the auction rates.
The three-month bills were being offered with effective yields ranging from 11.465 to 11.55 percent and bidded between 11.55 to 11.70 percent.

The six-month bills were offered between 11.75 and 11.90 and bidded out between 11.95 to 12.025 percent, and one-year bills were trading at 12.55 to 11.625 on the offer side and 12.675 to 12.825 percent on the bid side.
"The secondary market was quiet. We have an almost equal amount of buyers and sellers," another trader said.
